description.narrative:
Pursuant to the proposal submitted by ACF dated on the 08 September 2022 to Sida, the proposed objectives for the following periods from 2023-2025 have been updated to previous objectives which are assessed timely relevant to the current labor context in Cambodia. The main objective of the contribution focuses on the "Contribution to higher productivity, labour sector stability, and better living conditions for workers" with the following sub-objectives to achieve target results.
1. Improved social dialogue and labour relations through accessible, transparent, and well-functioning labour dispute resolution system.
2. Increased participation and capacity of industrial relations beneficiaries in dispute prevention and resolution processes in selected enterprises and at the Arbitration Council.
3. Enhanced institutional integrity and sustainability of the Arbitration Council, Arbitration Council Foundation and their services.
4. Gender equality awareness is raised among ACF staff, Secretariat officials, Arbitrators, and ACFs beneficiaries.

Kärnstödet till Arbitration Council Foundation för att genomföra programmet "Strengthening Industrial Relations and Labour Market Conditions in Cambodia" varar under perioden 2019-2024. Den föreslagna insatsen syftar till att stärka industriella relationer och arbetsmarknadsvillkor genom social dialog och ett välfungerande, trovärdigt skiljedomssystem för arbetstvister i Kambodja genom 1) tvistlösning, 2) partnerskap och uppsökande verksamhet med intressenter, 3) ökad institutionell integritet och trovärdighet, och 4) institutionell kapacitetsstärkning och samarbete med arbetsministeriet.

The core support to Arbitration Council Foundation to carry out the Programme "Strengthening Industrial Relations and Labour Market Conditions in Cambodia" lasts for a period from 2019-2024. The proposed intervention aims at strengthening industrial relations and labour market conditions through social dialogue and well-functioning, credible labour dispute arbitration system in Cambodia by 1) labour dispute resolution, 2) partnership and outreach with stakeholders, 3) increased institutional integrity and credibility, and 4) institutional strengthening and collaboration with the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training.

Summary of results for the agreement period:
Component 1: Labour Dispute Resolution Between 2021 and 2024, the AC resolved 193 labour dispute cases, directly benefiting 79,933 workers. In 2024 alone, 12 dispute cases were processed, addressing 34 distinct issues. This represents a 42% decline in cases compared to 2023. Of the 12 cases, 11 resulted in arbitral awards, and 1 was resolved through agreement during the hearing. The Council maintained a long-term success rate of 76%. On average, it took 25 days to resolve a case in 2024, slightly above the 2023 average of 21 days, yet consistent with the historical average of 22 days (2003-2024).
Component 2: Partnership and Stakeholder Outreach and Training In 2024, the Dispute Prevention and Resolution Program (DPRP) exceeded expectations with participation from 10 enterprises, surpassing the target of 8. The program delivered 40 training sessions to 192 participants (96 women), located in Phnom Penh and four provinces. Evaluation results indicated that 85% of participants met the minimum knowledge benchmark, exceeding the target of 75%. The program built practical skills and fostered dialogue among employers, unions, and worker representatives, contributing to a more sound workplace environment.
Component 3: Institutional Integrity and Sustainability During the latter half of 2024, ACF engaged in discussions with the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training (MoLVT) regarding institutional development, funding, and a possible relocation to new offices and integration of ACF into the ministerial structure of the MoLVT as the MoLVT expressed intentions to nationalize the AC and ACF. ACF has proactively prepared for relocation to the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) building and presented a detailed proposal including functional office designs and a budget plan. Discussions on long-term sustainability and maintaining independence has been conducted .
Component 4: Gender Equality ACF made efforts in advancing gender equality within the organization. In collaboration with ILO/Better Factories Cambodia, ACF conducted capacity-building sessions focused on gender equality for staff and arbitrators. Furthermore, training on workplace harassment was provided to 23 participants (15 women), including staff and arbitrators.
Summary Across all four components, ACF demonstrated efforts to improve labour dispute resolution processes, stakeholder engagement, institutional resilience, and gender equality. Despite challenges such as declining case referrals and pending regulatory frameworks, ACF maintained its efforts to service delivery.
